The young woman is 18, but yesterday, when she gave us an interview, she seemed much older. Her name is Adimar da Cunha Baia. She lives in Vila 3 Amigas, on Rua 26 de Setembro, near N. Itororó; she prefers that we not give the house number.
She is very tense and nervous, with a certain restraint in her voice, as though she would rather not speak. She still feels feverish and her body repeatedly trembles. Adimar has been like this since last Tuesday, when at 23.00 she was struck by a beam of light, mainly on her breasts, causing her to faint a few seconds later.
It happened in her own house as she was turning on the kitchen light. She says that a strong, hot beam descended through a gap in the roof and struck her forehead and breasts. She tried to see something but could not. It lasted a fraction of a second, and as the beam faded it turned red; when it first touched her, its color resembled an ordinary household lamp. Her body's reaction followed immediately. Her whole body reddened, her breasts turned purple as though they had been sucked, and then her body began trembling and contorting. She had only enough time to run to bed, where the contortions continued; shortly afterward she fainted.
Adimar was then taken to Hospital Belém, where doctors gave her injections and later discharged her. During her stay from one to four on Wednesday morning, the doctors who treated her refused to give any statement about the incident and kept her in an isolated room, allowing no visitors, not even relatives.
Only Adimar, her brother and Merian da Silva Cunha, who has lived with the family for a long time, were home at the time. Adimar's father had gone to work at night and her mother had gone to a brother-in-law's house. Merian came to help Adimar and also saw the “beam,” but was not struck by it.
